txt: A metallic drawer slides out from under the seat and clicks into place. The tools inside are neatly organized.
An audio-assault descends full force on you. Sonic daggers fly forth from the Kineema's speakers. The soundwaves would slice you if they could.
As you tap on the gauge, the indicator pin jerks as if startled. It's in the large orange sector, indicating the engine is warm. Next to the gauge is a red switch labelled HEAT.
As you tap on the gauge, the indicator pin jerks as if startled. It's in the small blue sector, indicating the engine is cold. Next to the gauge is a red switch labelled HEAT.
Before you stands a motor carriage. The bodywork is covered in blue and white livery bearing the number 57.
Even at a standstill the uni-body Coupris Kineema looks sleek and dynamic. The cabin is tilted frontward to give it a more aggressive *hunched* look.
Glowing lights on a dashboard emerge out of nothingness.
I'm good, cherished and cared for, in the hands of a tending owner.
If, when a motor-carriage's engine was ignited, it could drive by its own accord off to a high mountain and there write a song -- perhaps it'd be something like what you're hearing now.
In the cabin you are welcomed by a set of steering levers, a radio-microphone on a hook, a pull-out toolbox under the seat, and the soft glow of the fuel pre-heater gauge.
In the cabin you see a set of steering levers, a radio on a hook, a pull-out toolbox and the soft glow of the fuel pre-heater gauge.
In the upholstered cabin of Lieutenant Kitsuragi's motor carriage, seated in the driver's basket. The air is thick with leatherworks and heavy fuel oil. Cold water runs down your chin.
Inside you see a set of steering levers, a radio-microphone, a pull-out toolbox, and the soft glow of the fuel pre-heater gauge.
It requires no adjustment. The radio is already set to Speedfreaks FM.
It's robust, weatherproof and well made. Police issue -- blue.
No reply. Only the mindless drone of static, crawling through the air.
Silence.
Something is wrong. Only static hisses through the speaker.
The button stays in the dash for a few seconds, then jumps out and... nothing happens.
The cage at the back of the motor carriage looks rather uncomfortable. Four shiny hubcaps are stacked against the seat. Their silver edges sparkle in the dark.
The dashboard lights up with orange glow. The rounds per minute gauge jumps and the engine of the Coupris Kineema comes to life with a whiny growl.
The frequency tableau lights up and a green button labelled PRIMELINE glows like a feline eye... and then you hear something.
The handles are long and sleek. *Snap-snap* go the cutters in your hand.
The lights unfold with a little click, casting electrical light onto the ground before the vehicle.
The prybar feels nice and cold in your hand. Heavier than you'd think.
The pull-out toolbox slides back into its nest. Pre-heater gauge casts a warm glow on the steering levers and the radio on its hook.
The radio DJ stops. For a moment it seems like he has ran out of things to say...
The silence is almost deafening after you flick off the switch, severing the connection.
The soft purr of electrical kittens -- radio waves cast far and wide over the metropolis. A woman's voice greets you through the static:
The water is cold, silvery  -- the stuff of *life itself* as it pours down your parched throat. The pounding in your head recedes, the darkness parts.
The white suede feels luxurious under the touch and the metal clutch handle so very familiar in your palm...
Uhm... When Lieutenant Kitsuragi is here? It's his MC.
Vapour emanates from the large engine on the back of the vehicle. It hasn't had time to cool off yet.
With greedy gulps, you down half a litre of cold water. Some of it spills on the driver's seat -- the lieutenant pays no heed to it.
